abstract: integrates sensory and motor information and transmits signals to the muscles via motor neurons. The sole cerebellar output neurons, Purkinje cells (PCs), receive two main inputs from climbing fibers (CFs) and parallel fibers (PFs), which are the axons of granule cells (GCs). The serine/threonine kinase liver kinase B1 (LKB1) regulates GC migration; however, its role in PF synapses remains unclear. We generated a novel strain of mice with a LKB1 conditional knockout (cKO) in GCs during the postnatal period to investigate the presynaptic function of LKB1. LKB1 cKO mice exhibited progressive declines in motor coordination, whereas general locomotor activity was preserved. Morphological analysis revealed shrinkage of the cerebellar molecular layer with increased microglial density, suggesting degenerative remodeling of PF-PC synapses. Conventional electron microscopy showed a slight increase in the PF terminal area in LKB1 cKO mice, whereas three-dimensional reconstructions revealed no significant differences in bouton morphology except for an increased mitochondrial volume ratio. In contrast, the proportion of PF boutons forming multiple synapses with PC spines was higher in LKB1 cKO mice than in controls, potentially altering synaptic inputs to PCs and contributing to downstream changes in cerebellar output and reduced presynaptic occupancy at neuromuscular junctions. These findings highlight the importance of LKB1 in GCs for maintaining PF-PC synaptic remodeling and cerebellar circuit integrity, which may contribute to motor coordination.
